Recent field surveys of the Sordid rubberlip, Plectorhinchus sordidus, have provided detailed life-history measurements for this commercially important haemulid from the western Pacific. Neonates emerge from demersal eggs at an extremely small size, with the wet weight at birth estimated at 0.00032 grams [Wwb = 0.00032 grams], a value derived from the average egg diameter of 0.85 millimeters. The embryonic incubation period is notably brief; egg hatching occurs after only 5 days [ab = 5 days] when water temperatures are maintained at 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C], reflecting the rapid developmental rates typical of tropical teleost larvae. This short yolk-dependent phase is followed by an exotrophic transition as the prolarvae begin exogenous feeding. These early life-history traits, characterized by a minute neonatal mass and swift hatching time, position the species towards the fast end of the life-history continuum among reef fishes, prioritizing rapid dispersal and high fecundity over per-offspring investment.

As growing juveniles recruit to benthic habitats, they initiate a prolonged period of somatic growth that culminates in a substantial adult body size. The maximum recorded fork length for this species is 60 centimeters [Li = 60 centimeters], a size that places Plectorhinchus sordidus among the larger members of its genus. Morphometric relationships derived from field collections indicate that this asymptotic length corresponds to a theoretical ultimate wet weight of 2876 grams [Wwi = 2876 grams], calculated from the species-specific length-weight conversion. The transition to sexual maturation does not occur until individuals have attained a fork length of 26 centimeters [Lp = 26 centimeters], at which point the corresponding body mass is approximately 238 grams [Wwp = approximately 238 grams]. This pubertal size threshold represents roughly 43 percent of the ultimate fork length, a pattern broadly consistent with the maturation schedules observed in other iteroparous haemulid fishes that delay reproduction until a substantial portion of somatic growth is complete.

In reproductively active adults, the gonadosomatic index (GSI) reaches 5.8% [GSI = 5.8%] under thermal conditions of 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C]. This value was obtained from gravid individuals collected during the peak spawning season. The life-history schedule of Plectorhinchus sordidus is further characterized by a maximum lifespan of 4015 days [am = 4015 days], which corresponds to 11 years, derived from tag-recapture studies and otolith ageing at 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C].

Comparative analysis with other haemulids reveals that the size at puberty for Plectorhinchus sordidus is reached at a fork length of 26 cm [Lp = 26 cm], a threshold that aligns closely with values reported for the related species Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides. The mass at which individuals achieve this pubertal fork length is 238 grams [Wwp = 238 grams], a body weight that represents a substantial accumulation of somatic tissue prior to the onset of gametogenesis. In contrast, the maximum body mass of 2876 grams [Wwi = 2876 grams] is attained only after many years of sustained growth, with the asymptotic size being a strong predictor of lifetime fecundity in this lineage. The growth trajectory from the pubertal mass of 238 grams [Wwp = 238 grams] to the ultimate mass of 2876 grams [Wwi = 2876 grams] represents a greater than tenfold increase in wet weight during the adult phase, underscoring the continued allocation of resources to somatic growth well beyond the onset of reproductive maturity.

The ecological context of these measurements is informed by the thermal regime of the species' coral reef habitat. All embryonic and early larval development occurs at a stable water temperature of 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C], a condition that supports the rapid 5-day hatching period (5 days) [ab = 5 days] noted earlier. Field observations confirm that this same thermal environment is maintained throughout the species' lifespan, with long-term records indicating that the maximum documented age of 4015 days [am = 4015 days] is achieved without significant deviation from this baseline temperature at a temperature of 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C]. The gonadosomatic index was 5.8% [GSI = 5.8%] under optimal thermal conditions at a temperature of 27.1 °C [T = 27.1 °C]. These collective data, including the ultimate fork length of 60 cm [Li = 60 cm] and the pubertal fork length of 26 cm [Lp = 26 cm], provide a robust empirical foundation for understanding the life-history ecology of this important reef fish species.
